First thing is we removed duplicate nucleotide accessions from the assemblies
```python
import pandas as pd
import re

# === Load your data ===
file_path = "complete_homarine_catabolic_operons_second_round_genome_metadata_and_taxonomy.tsv"
df = pd.read_csv(file_path, sep="\t")

# === Function to extract numeric portion from Nucleotide Accession ===
def extract_numeric_part(accession):
    match = re.search(r'(\d+)\.\d+$', str(accession))
    return int(match.group(1)) if match else -1

# Add a column with extracted number for sorting
df["accession_num"] = df["Nucleotide.Accession"].apply(extract_numeric_part)

# Find the max accession for each Assembly
max_accession_per_assembly = df.loc[
    df.groupby("Assembly")["accession_num"].idxmax()
][["Assembly", "Nucleotide.Accession"]]

# Keep all rows for the max accession of each Assembly
main_df = df.merge(max_accession_per_assembly, on=["Assembly", "Nucleotide.Accession"], how="inner")

# Filter out all others
filtered_df = df[~df.index.isin(main_df.index)]

# === Optional: Count assemblies ===
print("Unique Assemblies in main:", main_df["Assembly"].nunique())
print("Unique Assemblies in filtered:", filtered_df["Assembly"].nunique())

# === Save outputs ===
main_df.drop(columns=["accession_num"]).to_csv("main_filtered_accessions_corrected.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
filtered_df.drop(columns=["accession_num"]).to_csv("removed_accessions_corrected.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
```

Then we searched for the different operons in the assemblies
```python
import pandas as pd

# === Load your data ===
df = pd.read_csv("main_filtered_accessions_corrected.tsv", sep="\t")

# === Keep only necessary columns for speed ===
cols_needed = ["Assembly", "organism.name", "gene.name", "start", "subject",
               "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species"]

df_trimmed = df[cols_needed]

# === Filter only 'hom' genes and sort by genome position ===
hom_df = df_trimmed[df_trimmed["gene.name"].str.startswith("hom", na=False)]
hom_sorted = hom_df.sort_values(by=["Assembly", "start"])

# === Group by Assembly and extract gene cluster + metadata ===
summary_data = []
grouped = hom_sorted.groupby("Assembly")

for assembly, group in grouped:
    gene_cluster = "".join(group["gene.name"].dropna())
    first_row = group.iloc[0]
    subject_ids = ";".join(sorted(set(group["subject"].dropna().astype(str))))
    summary_data.append({
        "Assembly": assembly,
        "organism": first_row["organism.name"],
        "gene_cluster": gene_cluster,
        "subject": subject_ids,
        "phylum": first_row["phylum"],
        "class": first_row["class"],
        "order": first_row["order"],
        "family": first_row["family"],
        "genus": first_row["genus"],
        "species": first_row["species"]
    })

# === Create final dataframe and sort ===
summary_df = pd.DataFrame(summary_data)
summary_df_sorted = summary_df.sort_values(by=["class", "gene_cluster"])

# === Save to file ===
summary_df_sorted.to_csv("homarine_operon_cluster_summary_by_assembly_corrected.csv", index=False)

# Done!
print("✅ Finished. Summary saved as 'homarine_operon_cluster_summary_by_assembly.csv'")
```

Sort genes lexicographically to get the canonical cluster (eg. ABCD and DCBA are the same)
```python
#hom_genes_lexicographically.py
import pandas as pd

# Load the CSV file
input_path = "/mnt/c/SynologyDrive/UW/UW_Anitra_Ingalls/Homarine_project/Data/metadata_extract/homarine_operon_cluster_summary_by_assembly_corrected_mod.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(input_path)

# Function to generate canonical form of gene clusters
def true_canonical_cluster(cluster_str):
    genes = list(cluster_str)  # assumes each gene is a single character
    forward = ''.join(genes)
    reverse = ''.join(genes[::-1])
    return min(forward, reverse)

# Apply canonical cluster transformation
df["canonical_cluster"] = df["gene_cluster"].apply(true_canonical_cluster)

# Save updated file
output_path = "/mnt/c/SynologyDrive/UW/UW_Anitra_Ingalls/Homarine_project/Data/metadata_extract/homarine_operon_cluster_summary_with_true_canonical.csv"
df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

print("Canonical cluster column added. Output saved to:")
print(output_path)
```


Finally, we created a figure with the different operons and their respective taxons in order and class
```python
#plot_sorted_hom_genes_canonical.py
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# === Load the data ===
summary_df = pd.read_csv("homarine_operon_cluster_summary_with_true_canonical.csv")

# === Prepare count data ===
class_counts = summary_df.groupby(["canonical_cluster", "class"]).size().reset_index(name="count")
order_counts = summary_df.groupby(["canonical_cluster", "order"]).size().reset_index(name="count")

# === Plot style ===
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# === Plot 1: Gene Cluster by Class (log y-scale) ===
plt.figure(figsize=(20, 10), constrained_layout=True)
sns.barplot(data=class_counts, x="canonical_cluster", y="count", hue="class", dodge=False)
plt.yscale("log")
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.xlabel("Gene Cluster (hom)")
plt.ylabel("Count (log scale)")
plt.title("Homarine Gene Cluster Distribution by Class")
plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)
plt.savefig("gene_cluster_by_class_canonical.pdf")
plt.close()

# === Plot 2: Gene Cluster by Order (log y-scale) ===
plt.figure(figsize=(20, 10), constrained_layout=True)
sns.barplot(data=order_counts, x="canonical_cluster", y="count", hue="order", dodge=False)
plt.yscale("log")
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.xlabel("Gene Cluster (hom)")
plt.ylabel("Count (log scale)")
plt.title("Homarine Gene Cluster Distribution by Order")
plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)
plt.savefig("gene_cluster_by_order_canonical.pdf")
plt.close()
```
